A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage BokehDepth framework despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bokeh-rendering and metric-depth experiments, component ablations, and supplementary inference-step results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparator results, sensitivity and control experiments, computational measurements, and depth-error analyses.

M1.justification: The calibrated-K bokeh adapter, FLUX-Kontext backbone, and DSFA spatial/focus attention with FiLM are retained, alongside the unchanged depth decoder and losses. The new alternative bokeh sources are experimental controls, not changes to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: The training datasets, evaluation datasets, and bokeh-rendering and metric-depth tasks are retained. Aperture-Dataset remains in Appendix B.3 despite disappearing from the shortened main-text description. New KITTI sweeps and IBims-1 analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DiffCamera and GenFocus. New Table 4 compares against Deep-Optics, DFF-DFV, 2HDED:Net, DAIF-Net and SDNet on NYUv2. The Stage-2 ablation also adds predicted-depth BokehMe and raw FLUX.1-Kontext comparisons, substantially expanding comparator coverage.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include stack-size/blur-range sweeps, alternative bokeh-source controls, and pixel-weighted IBims-1 metrics with edge masks and depth bins. The DfD comparison explicitly uses RGB-D-rendered stacks for competitors versus image-generated stacks for BokehDepth. New cost profiles use 30 diffusion steps, whereas retained Appendix F.1 specifies 10 for all stack generation; this ambiguity does not establish that existing benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and inference-step ablations, v2 tests stack size and blur range, sparse versus dense rendering geometry, and whether uncalibrated generator outputs provide useful cues. It also adds computational scaling and quantitative boundary/depth-range analyses in Section 5.3 and Appendices F–G.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests. The theoretical estimator-variance discussion does not provide uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: Original main-table and inference-step scores are retained, apart from equivalent rounding. Numerous comparison, control, sweep, cost and error-analysis results are added. New EBB! entries place GenFocus and DiffCamera above BokehDepth in SSIM: 0.886 and 0.867 versus 0.856. New IBims-1 analysis reports baseline/DSFA MAE of 0.3518/0.1925. The extended sparse-BokehMe result is 0.095 AbsRel in Table 10, inconsistent with 0.094 in retained Table 5.

T1.justification: The principal proposition and appendix proof are retained. Appendix F.2 newly asserts an O(1/(N Var(K))) variance rate to explain sweep design. This added theoretical claim is not reconciled with the retained through-origin estimator's dependence on the sum of squared K values.

C1.justification: The revised abstract adds inconsistent metric scale in diffusion-based depth models as a central problem, explicitly distinguishing these models from feed-forward estimators. The two-stage contributions and principal rendering and metric-depth improvement claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing gains to dense, calibrated defocus rather than generator artifacts, interprets stack sensitivity and depth-dependent gains, and argues for inexpensive inference after caching. It replaces v1 Section 14's decoupled-training/no-feedback limitation with Appendix I's uncertainty about video, moving scenes, exposure changes, rolling shutter and focus drift.

D1.justification: Tables 6 and 9 newly disclose parameter counts, latency and memory measurements. The revision clarifies sparse LiDAR and dense predicted-depth inputs for BokehMe controls and documents the 0.001-meter improvement-overlay threshold. Existing training schedules, hardware, data-conversion details and project-page access are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GenFocus, several DfD methods and diffusion distillation, while removing some older background citations. It explicitly positions its single-image input against competitors' RGB-D-rendered focal stacks. The broad related-work survey and positioning relative to Bokeh Diffusion and IP-Adapter remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the Stage-1 background and training subsections are condensed into Section 3.1, and terminology and appendix organization are revised. Most existing methodological, related-work and supplementary prose retains its structure and meaning.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison, resource, sensitivity and error-analysis tables and expands the existing ablation display. It substantially reformats the paper, converts the appendix to one column, and resizes or relocates figures. The last example from v1 Figure 1 moves into v2 Figure 6 rather than being removed.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, source controls, sensitivity tests and localized error analyses strengthen empirical support, while resource tables make practical costs assessable. These benefits are tempered by new reporting problems: unreconciled 10-versus-30-step descriptions, a 'nearly identical' cached-latency claim despite 0.045 versus 0.114 seconds in Table 6, and the variance-rate mismatch in Appendix F.2. The net improvement is useful but limited.
